title: Anonymous Functions
summary: Functions without a name, written inline as `function(...) end` or `(...) -> ...`. The standard way to pass behavior to event connections, task.spawn, and callbacks.

syntax:
-- classic form
part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    print(hit.Name)
end)

-- arrow syntax (Luau)
local double = (n) -> n * 2
local greet = (name) -> `Hello, {name}!`

-- multi-statement arrow
local clamp01 = (x) -> math.clamp(x, 0, 1)

details.heading: They are values
details.body: An anonymous function is just a function value that was never given a variable name. You can still assign it: `local fn = function() end` — that's how 'anonymous' functions get names.

explanation.whatItIs: A function you create right where you need it, without inventing a name for it. Most often used as a *callback*: 'here is what to do when X happens'.
explanation.whyItExists: Event-driven Roblox code constantly needs 'do this when that happens'. One-off handlers don't deserve top-level names.
whenToUse: Comparators: `table.sort(t, function(a, b) return a > b end)`
whenNotToUse: If the callback is longer than ~10 lines, promote it to a named local function — stack traces and readability improve hugely
If you need to disconnect the connection later, a named function + stored connection is easier to manage
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
button.Activated:Connect(
    function()                -- "the thing to do"
        print("Clicked!")
    end
)
```
You're handing Roblox a sealed envelope of behavior. It opens it when the event fires.
tips: Anonymous functions capture locals from their surroundings (closures) — that's how they see your `player` variable
Arrow syntax `(x) -> x * 2` is concise but only for single expressions
commonMistakes: Passing a *call* instead of the function: `Connect(onClick())` runs immediately and passes nil. Write `Connect(onClick)` or `Connect(function() onClick() end)`
Forgetting `end` — anonymous functions need their own closing `end`
Deeply nested anonymous functions making code unreadable — extract names

examples.title: The classic Roblox callback
examples.code:
local button = script.Parent

button.Activated:Connect(function()
    print("Button clicked by someone!")
end)

-- Same thing, named version (easier to read once it grows):
local function onClick()
    print("Button clicked by someone!")
end
button.Activated:Connect(onClick)
examples.commonMistake: `button.Activated:Connect(onClick())` would call onClick *now* and connect its return value (nil) — a very common beginner bug.

examples.title: Arrow functions
examples.code:
local double = (n) -> n * 2
local shout = (text) -> string.upper(text) .. "!"

print(double(21))       --> 42
print(shout("hi"))      --> HI!

local numbers = {3, 1, 2}
table.sort(numbers, (a, b) -> a > b)
print(numbers[1])       --> 3
